stem.text: On the day of a sale, customers enter a department store at a rate modeled by \( E(t) = 90 + 70e^{-(t - 3)^{2}/4} \) customers per hour, and customers leave the store at a rate modeled by \( L(t) = \dfrac{150t^{2}}{t^{2} + 9} \) customers per hour, where \( t \) is the number of hours after the store opens and \( 0 \le t \le 8 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 30 customers in the store.

parts.prompt: Show that more than 950 customers enter the store during the interval \( 0 \le t \le 8 \).

worked_solution.text: The number of customers who enter is the integral of the entry rate.
Evaluate on the calculator and compare with 950.

points.criterion: Writes the definite integral of E(t) from t = 0 to t = 8.
Evaluates the integral as about 963.888 customers and concludes that more than 950 customers enter.

parts.prompt: Show that there are more than 390 customers in the store at time \( t = 4 \).

worked_solution.text: The number in the store at t = 4 is the starting number plus the integral of the net rate.
Evaluate on the calculator and compare with 390.

points.criterion: Writes the number at t = 4 as 30 plus the definite integral of E(t) - L(t) from t = 0 to t = 4, or as 30 plus the integral of E minus the integral of L over that interval.
Evaluates the number as about 391.729 customers, including the starting 30, and concludes that it is more than 390.

parts.prompt: Show that the greatest number of customers in the store at any time during \( 0 \le t \le 8 \) is less than 420.

worked_solution.text: Let N(t) be the number of customers in the store, so N'(t) = E(t) - L(t). Solve E(t) - L(t) = 0 on the calculator. The only solution in the interval is t = a, and E(t) - L(t) changes from positive to negative there.
The greatest number occurs at t = 0, t = a, or t = 8. Since N increases on 0 <= t <= a and decreases on a <= t <= 8, the greatest value is N(a).
Evaluate on the calculator, using the stored value of a, and compare with 420.

points.criterion: Writes the number at the time of the maximum as 30 plus the definite integral of E(t) - L(t) from t = 0 to t = 5.151, the solution of E(t) = L(t) (a letter set to that value, or more decimal places, is also accepted).

Finds t = 5.151 from E(t) = L(t) and justifies that the greatest number occurs there, because E(t) - L(t) changes from positive to negative at t = 5.151 and it is the only such time, or by comparing the values at t = 0, t = 5.151 and t = 8 (30, 418.499 and 339.299).
Evaluates the greatest number as about 418.499 customers and concludes that it is less than 420.

parts.prompt: Show that the average rate at which customers leave the store over the interval \( 4 \le t \le 8 \) is less than 120 customers per hour.

worked_solution.text: The average leaving rate is the integral of L over the interval divided by its length.
Evaluate on the calculator and compare with 120.

points.criterion: Writes the average leaving rate as 1/4 times the definite integral of L(t) from t = 4 to t = 8.
Evaluates the average as about 117.968 customers per hour (or the integral as about 471.871 customers and compares it with 4 times 120 = 480) and concludes that the average is less than 120.
